title: Paris: Pope Leo XIV to celebrate Mass before huge crowd
summary: Around 600,000 people have registered to attend a Mass at the Place de la Concorde, near the Champs-Elysees. Pope Leo XIV is on a four-day visit to France.

image.caption: Around 600,000 people have been registered to attend the open-air mass with Pope Leo XIVImage: Gonzalo Fuentes/REUTERS

blocks.text: Pope Leo XIV on Saturday will celebrate Mass for hundreds of thousands of worshippers in central Paris.
In the region of 600,000 people have registered to attend the afternoon Mass at the Place de la Concorde, near the Champs-Elysees.
The service is expected to take place from 3:00 p.m. local time (1300 GMT).

blocks.caption: People began gathering hours before the start of the mass in central ParisImage: Gonzalo Fuentes/REUTERS

blocks.text: Leo's first trip to France since becoming pope
Pope Leo is on a four-day visit to France that will see him in Paris, Lourdes and Metz. It's also his first visit to France since becoming pope last year.
Crowds began queuing hours before the service was due to begin, with many parents and children among those hoping to catch a glimpse of the leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics.
"It's a big event, we've come to share the Christian fervour," teacher Sylvie Leclerc told the AFP news agency.
"You don't hear much from us Catholics, but now we're going to make some noise! But to proclaim love, peace, joy," she added.
Earlier on Saturday, the pope visited a social center and later met with adults who had recently been baptized.

On Friday, around 300,000 people gathered to see the pontiff as he waved from his popemobile on the way to the restored Notre Dame Cathedral, which had to be restored after a devastating fire in 2019.
French President Emmanuel Macron will not attend the Mass, however, far-right leader Marine Le Pen and centrist Edouard Philippe have confirmed their attendance.
